title: return_sampling_mask=True has two independent request-level preconditions (temperature > 0 and top_k > 0) that are reported one at a time, and only after the engine is already running
body: Starting an engine with `return_sampling_mask=True` imposes **two independent preconditions on every request's `SamplingParams`**, but they are enforced separately and discovered sequentially: A caller who does the natural thing — construct `SamplingParams(temperature=...)` without `top_k` — satisfies the first check, then fails the second, and only learns the complete contract by triggering two separate errors. Nothing documents both conditions together, and neither check runs when the engine is configured, even though `return_sampling_mask` is an **engine-level** flag set at construction time: the incompatibility is only detectable per request, at `add_request` time. Two distinct problems: 1. **The preconditions are split across separate raises.** Both belong to the same `return_sampling_mask` feature and are known statically at request construction. Raising them one at a time forces trial-and-error to discover the contract; a single error listing all unmet preconditions (`temperature > 0`, `top_k > 0`) would be actionable in one round-trip. 2. **The check happens too late to help the operator.** `return_sampling_mask` is set on the engine, not the request. If a server is started with `return_sampling_mask=True`, then *every* request must carry `top_k > 0`; a client that sends the default `SamplingParams(temperature=0.7)` is rejected at request time, after the engine has been built and the deployment cut over. At minimum this deserves a startup-time warning (or an explicit note in the flag's help text), and arguably a config-time validation of the combination. Note the rejections themselves are **clean** — the request is rejected with `ValueError` and the engine survives (verified: a subsequent valid request on the same engine succeeds). This report is about the error contract and the validation timing, not about a crash. A ready-made driver for these three cases on a single engine is in `repro_return_sampling_mask.py`. Either of: - **One combined, actionable erro
label: bug

title: jit_monitor_mode="error" kills the engine on the first real request for hybrid mamba models — JIT warmup never covers precopy_mamba_align_fused_kernel
body: vLLM's JIT monitor (`vllm/utils/jit_monitor.py`) is activated at the end of `compile_or_warm_up_model()`; with `jit_monitor_mode="error"` every monitored Triton JIT compilation during inference raises. For a **hybrid mamba model** (`LiquidAI/LFM2-8B-A1B`, conv + SSM + full-attention), the built-in startup warmup is *not* sufficient to keep that promise: the engine completes the full "JIT kernel warmup (154 compile keys)" pass and CUDA-graph capture (56/56), then **dies on the first real inference step**: Root cause — a warmup coverage gap, not a user misconfiguration: 1. The per-step mamba pre-copy kernel `precopy_mamba_align_fused_kernel` is a **raw `@triton.jit` kernel** invoked directly as `precopy_mamba_align_fused_kernel[grid](...)` (`vllm/v1/worker/mamba_utils.py:1212`, called from `preprocess_mamba` on every `execute_model`). It is not a registered `VllmJitKernel`, so the JIT warmup registry (`vllm/model_executor/warmup/jit_warmup.py`, which only pre-compiles registered kernels — the 154 keys above) never compiles it. 2. CUDA-graph capture does not execute it either: the pre-copy runs outside the captured region, so the first real `execute_model` is its first-ever invocation. 3. The monitor is already active at that point → triton's post-compile hook → `_handle_jit_event` → `raise RuntimeError` (`jit_monitor.py:134`) → **the EngineCore process dies**, and the client only sees an opaque `EngineDeadError`; the actionable message is buried in EngineCore stderr. Net effect: enabling a *diagnostic* mode turns a latency-spike advisory into a fatal, unrecoverable crash on the very first request, deterministically, for every hybrid mamba model. Reproduced across 4 distinct configs × 2 variants (`mamba_cache_dtype` bfloat16/float16/float32, ±`use_fp64_gumbel`, ±`disable_hybrid_kv_cache_manager`) — all identical; the same configs *without* `jit_monitor_mode` run fine. The engine survives inference in `jit_monitor_mode="error"`: the per-step raw triton kernels of suppor
label: bug

title: fp8 kernel selection discards per-kernel rejection reasons — quantization="fp8_per_channel" surfaces as a misleading "Requires SM89+ for Cutlass FP8" with no indication of what actually failed
body: `quantization="fp8_per_channel"` (online PTPC: per-token-per-channel weight scale + dynamic per-token activation scale, `kFp8StaticChannelSym` → `Fp8PtpcOnlineLinearMethod`) passes config validation, but the model load then dies inside `create_weights` with: Two problems, both independent of which GPU model is used: 1. **The real per-kernel rejection reasons are discarded, so the error cannot be acted on.** `init_fp8_linear_kernel` walks `_POSSIBLE_FP8_KERNELS` (FlashInfer → Cutlass → B12xTensor → PerTensorTorch → ChannelWiseTorch → Marlin → …) and collects a `failure_reason_list` for the candidates it rejects. But Marlin's `can_implement` accepts everything, so `choose_scaled_mm_linear_kernel` simply **returns Marlin** — the collected reasons are never surfaced. Only afterwards does the PTPC guard (`vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/online/fp8.py:386`) raise, with a message that names a generic capability requirement ("Requires SM89+ for Cutlass FP8") instead of saying *why FlashInfer and Cutlass were skipped for this configuration*. A user (and a bug report) cannot distinguish "this hardware genuinely lacks a PTPC-capable kernel" from "an earlier gate wrongly rejected the good kernels" — the message is identical in both cases. 2. **The guard fires too late.** It raises after `super().create_weights()` has already run, i.e. after the weights have been allocated in the quantized layout for a configuration that can never work. Model-independent — identical failure on `LiquidAI/LFM2-8B-A1B` (hybrid) and `stabilityai/stablelm-3b-4e1t` (dense), 2/2 each: the defect is in the kernel-selection / error-reporting path, not in the model. > Note on hardware: the `fp8_per_channel` path was also observed on an RTX 5880 Ada. If `cutlass_fp8_supported()` (→ `ops.cutlass_scaled_mm_supports_fp8(...)`) reports `False` on a device whose compute capability is already ≥ 8.9, that is an **additional** finding (the advertised fallback is unreachable); please see the probe output in
label: bug

title: enable_lora with max_lora_rank=320 crashes engine startup on MoE models — AssertionError: fused_moe_lora_one_shot supports max_lora_rank<=128
body: `max_lora_rank` accepts 256/320/512 as documented config values (`MaxLoRARanks = Literal[1, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 320, 512]`, `vllm/config/lora.py:27`), and `EngineArgs.create_engine_config()` accepts them. But on a **MoE model** (`allenai/OLMoE-1B-7B-0924-Instruct`, 64 experts), setting `enable_lora=True` with `max_lora_rank=320` crashes the engine during startup — in the dummy warmup forward, before any LoRA adapter is even loaded: The MoE fused LoRA triton path has a hard kernel capacity limit of 128, enforced only as a raw `assert` deep inside a torch custom op (`_run_fused_moe_lora_one_shot`, `vllm/lora/ops/triton_ops/fused_moe_lora_op.py:352`), reached via `triton_moe.py` → `punica_gpu.py` during the fused-MoE forward. Nothing reconciles the config-level `max_lora_rank` (which allows 512) against the selected MoE-LoRA backend's capacity (128), so a config-valid value produces an opaque `RuntimeError: Engine core initialization failed` with the assert only visible in EngineCore stderr. The same model with `max_lora_rank=128` starts and runs normally, confirming the trigger is exactly the rank value hitting the MoE kernel cap. No LoRA adapter request is needed — the engine dies during startup. Either the MoE LoRA path handles rank>128, or the invalid-for-backend combination is rejected cleanly at config-validation time with a descriptive error, e.g.: Currently the mismatch is only discovered as a raw kernel assert mid-warmup, and the user-visible error is an opaque engine-init failure. Config accepted → model loads → startup dummy forward through fused MoE → `apply_w13_lora` → `punica_wrapper.add_lora_w13` → `fused_moe_lora` → `_run_fused_moe_lora_one_shot` → `assert rank <= 128` fails → EngineCore dies → client sees `RuntimeError: Engine core initialization failed`. - vLLM: 0.31.0 (official wheel) - PyTorch: 2.13.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0, driver 580.82.07 - GPU: NVIDIA RTX 5880 Ada Generation (sm89, 47.4 GiB) - OS: Ubuntu 22.04.4 LTS (glibc 2.35), Python 3.12.13 -
label: bug

title: quantization="fp8" + kv_cache_dtype="float16" on a bf16 model crashes at startup — same flash-attn dtype assert as #60859, now on the online-quant path
body: For a **bfloat16** checkpoint (`allenai/OLMoE-1B-7B-0924-Instruct`) with **online fp8 quantization** (`quantization="fp8"`) and `kv_cache_dtype="float16"`, config validation passes, but the engine dies during startup memory profiling with the same raw kernel assert reported in #60859: Crash path: `determine_available_memory` → `profile_cudagraph_memory` → `capture_model(profile_only=True)` → `forward_fn(CUDAGraphMode.NONE)` → flash-attn `mha_varlen_fwd`. The point of this report: the missing dtype-compat validation is **not limited to plain bf16 checkpoints**. With online fp8 quantization the linear layers run quantized while attention still receives bf16 queries; nothing reconciles the triple (model dtype × quantization × kv_cache_dtype), and the FLASH_ATTN path again passes bf16 query tensors against fp16 KV cache without a cast. Control: the same model + `quantization="fp8"` **without** `kv_cache_dtype` runs fine (2/2) — causality is isolated to `kv_cache_dtype="float16"` on the fp8-quant path. Either the engine works (cast the query to the KV-cache dtype as the FLASHINFER path already does for fp8 KV), or the combination is rejected cleanly at config-validation time with a descriptive error, e.g.: Config accepted → EngineCore init → `profile_cudagraph_memory` → `capture_model(profile_only=True)` → raw CUDA kernel assert → `RuntimeError: Engine core initialization failed`. - vLLM: 0.31.0 (official wheel) - PyTorch: 2.13.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0, driver 580.82.07 - GPU: NVIDIA RTX 5880 Ada Generation (sm89, 47.4 GiB) - OS: Ubuntu 22.04.4 LTS (glibc 2.35), Python 3.12.13 - Found by a config-interaction test generator crossing `kv_cache_dtype` values with quantization methods on a bf16 MoE checkpoint. - Cross-check on the same model (2/2 attempts each): | config | outcome | |---|---| | quantization="fp8" only | OK | | quantization="fp8" + kv_cache_dtype="float16" | **RuntimeError: query and key must have the same dtype** | | (reference) plain bf16 + kv_cache_dtype="float1
label: bug

title: disable_hybrid_kv_cache_manager=True crashes engine startup on hybrid mamba models — ValueError: Failed to promote local KV cache specs to one unified type
body: For hybrid mamba-attention models (e.g. `LiquidAI/LFM2-8B-A1B`, conv + SSM + full-attention layers), setting the documented engine flag `disable_hybrid_kv_cache_manager=True` passes CPU-side config validation (`EngineArgs.create_engine_config()`), but the EngineCore process then dies during memory profiling: Crash path: `determine_available_memory` → `profile_cudagraph_memory` → `_init_minimal_kv_cache_for_profiling` → `get_kv_cache_groups` → `unify_hybrid_kv_cache_specs` → `_promote_local_kv_cache_specs` (`vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py:1901`). The trigger is precisely the **flag × hybrid-architecture** interaction (same GPU, same stack, ~30 configs probed): - The flag on 10+ **non-hybrid** models (bloom-560m, phi-2, opt-125m, Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct, OLMoE-1B-7B, Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B, ...) → accepted, engine runs. - The same hybrid model **without** the flag (including with suffix spec-decode + `mamba_cache_dtype` variants) → engine runs fine. - The minimal single-flag repro → crashes deterministically (2/2 independent attempts). So on hybrid models the flag is either not honored (the hybrid unification path runs anyway and then fails) or unsupported — either way the combination should be guarded at config-validation time, not discovered as a deep `ValueError` inside EngineCore memory profiling. Either the fallback (non-hybrid KV cache manager) is honored and the engine runs, or the combination is rejected cleanly at config time, e.g.: Config accepted → EngineCore init → `determine_available_memory` → `profile_cudagraph_memory` → `_init_minimal_kv_cache_for_profiling` → raw `ValueError` → client sees `RuntimeError: Engine core initialization failed`. - vLLM: 0.31.0 (official wheel) - PyTorch: 2.13.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0, driver 580.82.07 - GPU: NVIDIA RTX 5880 Ada Generation (sm89, 47.4 GiB) - OS: Ubuntu 22.04.4 LTS (glibc 2.35), Python 3.12.13 - Found by a config-interaction test generator probing engine flags against model architectures. - Cross-check of the flag across

title: NixlConnector: KV blocks released on lease expiry while remote READ in flight, decode silently consumes overwritten KV
body: **Env:** vLLM 0.30.0 (aed92ba5), NixlConnector 1P1D on one host, UCX (`UCX_TLS=tcp,cuda_copy`), Qwen2.5-0.5B, `--enforce-eager`, `--max-model-len 2048`. **Summary:** With the pull flow, the producer releases a request's KV blocks when `kv_lease_duration` expires, unconditionally — it does not matter whether a consumer read is still pending or about to be issued. The consumer side has no content/identity binding on the block descriptors it received earlier, so it reads whatever bytes now occupy those slots (they may belong to a newer request that reused them) and feeds them to the model with no error or warning. Output is silently wrong. **Repro (deterministic, no code changes):** 1. Start P (`kv_role=kv_producer`) and D (`kv_role=kv_consumer`). 2. Send a completion to P with `kv_transfer_params={"do_remote_decode": true, ...}` (max_tokens=1). Record the returned `kv_transfer_params` (remote_block_ids / remote_request_id). 3. Stall the decode engine for > `kv_lease_duration` (default 30 s). We used `SIGSTOP` on the decode processes to simulate an engine pause (GC / long step / scheduler stall); ~33.6 s total. 4. During the stall, P logs: `Releasing expired KV blocks for request <id> which were retrieved by 0 remote worker(s) before lease expired.` 5. Send new completions to P (same total token length) so the freed slots are reused and overwritten with different content. 6. Resume D and send the original completion to D with the recorded `kv_transfer_params`. 7. D performs the remote pull (`NIXL compatibility check passed` — the only check is the layout hash) and generates. The output continues *the other request's* content; there is no error or warning anywhere. **Results:** 5/5 trials with default `kv_lease_duration=30` and 5/5 with `kv_lease_duration=1`. Decode output in every trial followed the reused content ("foreign") rather than the request's own prompt. Controls: (a) decode computing the same prompt locally → correct output; (b) decode consuming the producer'
label: bug

title: Qwen Tool Calling errors - 3 parser issues
body: We investigated recurring Qwen tool-call failures on two identical GPUs in an OpenShift cluster. We found three problems and tested fixes for each. We would like to discuss where these fixes belong upstream; one already has an open PR. The second “parser bug” is technically in response assembly after parsing. The template problem concerns matching tool results to their calls. 1. **A = B:** Two identical NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q Workstation Edition GPUs, each running the same vLLM image, model and configuration. Both deployments reproduced the failures. We called them BAD and GOOD; initially, GOOD was just a copy. 2. **Build the tests:** With Codex, we built and ran a Python harness with four concurrent dialogs per system. Basic calls passed. Harder cases repeatedly failed, especially with reasoning enabled. 3. **Isolate technical failures:** We reduced the tests to an `echo_payload(text)` tool, fixed strings and tool histories. Replaying fixed output through the parser let us distinguish parser corruption from model mistakes. We compared Chat Completions and Responses. 4. **Upgrade GOOD:** We moved only GOOD from NVIDIA 26.06 to 26.09. Some older bugs disappeared, but reasoning markers inside tool arguments were still corrupted. 5. **Patch step by step:** We fixed marker handling, then incorrect cutoff reporting, then tool-result ordering. Each time, we restarted GOOD with patches loaded from the PVC and repeated the tests. No image rebuild was needed. 6. **Verify:** The final nonstreaming run covered 92 HTTP requests, including reasoning-enabled multicalls and follow-ups. The targeted regressions passed. Both GPUs reproduced the initial failures. Later patch comparisons were performed on GOOD, while BAD remained the baseline. Full details are collected in `env.txt`. The patched deployment used: - Image: `nvcr.io/nvidia/vllm:26.09-py3` - vLLM: `0.29.0+5013de39.dev` - Model: `unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4` - Parsers: `qwen3_coder` for tools, `qwen3` for reason
label: bug

title: MTP draft ignores target `--revision` (loads default branch) – regression vs 0.29, can crash with ZeroDivisionError
body: - vLLM 0.31.0 (Docker), works on 0.29 - Model: gittensor-model-hub/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4-RTX5090 with `--revision pre-final` With `--revision pre-final` and startup fails: For `method="mtp"`, `SpeculativeConfig.__post_init__` copies `model` (and `quantization`) from the target model config, but the draft `ModelConfig` is created with `revision=self.revision`, which is `None` unless set explicitly in the speculative config. The MTP draft therefore loads config (and weights) from the repo's default branch instead of the target's revision. Passing the revision explicitly fixes it: For `method="mtp"` (draft = target checkpoint), the draft should inherit the target's `revision` (and `code_revision`) when not set, the same way it inherits `model` and `quantization`. - If `n_predict` resolves to 0, the divisibility check should raise a readable error instead of `ZeroDivisionError`.
label: bug

title: Anthropic Messages silently drops unsupported system content blocks
body: The Anthropic Messages request schema accepts a list of content blocks in the top-level `system` field, including `image` blocks. During conversion to vLLM's internal chat request, `_convert_system_message()` only appends text blocks. The request is accepted, but the non-text system block is omitted from the converted prompt without an error. Start vLLM with a local model that can be used with the Anthropic Messages API. If the model has no chat template, provide a simple one such as the following in a file named `chat_template.jinja`: For example, start the server on loopback: Send a text-only control request and then the same request with an image block added to `system`: The Anthropic Messages API defines the top-level `system` field as a string or a list of text blocks. When a request contains unsupported non-text blocks in this field, vLLM should reject the request with a clear validation error or, at minimum, emit an explicit warning before discarding the unsupported content. This would be consistent with the warning-based compatibility approach adopted for the OpenAI-compatible API in PR #34072. Both requests returned HTTP 200 and the same token counts in the live test: `GET /health` returned HTTP 200 before and after the requests. The test confirms that the image block does not affect the request rendered and counted by this endpoint. It does not test generated model output. - [Anthropic request schema for Messages](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.31.0/vllm/entrypoints/anthropic/protocol.py#L36-L50) - [Anthropic request schema for token counting](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.31.0/vllm/entrypoints/anthropic/protocol.py#L321-L326) - [System-block conversion](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.31.0/vllm/entrypoints/anthropic/serving.py#L311-L346) Related issue and prior fix: - #33925 reported that the OpenAI-compatible endpoint accepted non-text system content. - PR #34072 introduced warnings for unsupported system content
label: bug

title: VLLM_MAX_AUDIO_CLIP_FILESIZE_MB=0 rejects non-empty audio
body: The security guide says setting any listed media limit to `0` disables that limit. However, setting `VLLM_MAX_AUDIO_CLIP_FILESIZE_MB=0` makes `AudioMediaIO` reject every non-empty encoded audio input. This means users cannot disable the compressed-file-size limit as the documentation describes. Run the following in an installed vLLM environment. The decoder is replaced with a stub so the test only exercises the size checks. Setting the limit to `0` should disable the compressed-file-size check, as described in the security guide. The separate audio-duration and decoded-audio-byte limits should remain in effect. With the limit set to `0`, both the bytes and base64 cases raise `VLLMValidationError` with `Maximum file size exceeded`, and the decoder stub is not called. With the control value set to `1`, both inputs pass the encoded-size checks and reach the decoder stub. The test uses a synthetic one-byte payload and does not claim it is valid audio. - [Security guide: media-size limits and zero-value behavior](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.31.0/docs/usage/security.md#L94-L105) - [Audio encoded-size checks](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.31.0/vllm/multimodal/media/audio.py#L540-L574)
label: bug

title: Severe output degeneration on SM120 with Apertus-70B FP8 in vLLM 0.25.1; v0.22.1 works after rollback
body:
Summary

We observed a severe text-generation correctness regression when upgrading from vLLM 0.22.1 to 0.25.1 using the same RedHatAI/Apertus-70B-Instruct-2509-FP8-dynamic checkpoint on an NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120).

The v0.25.1 engine initializes successfully, reports healthy, discovers the correct model, and returns HTTP 200 for inference. However, even a direct, non-streaming, temperature-zero request produces incoherent repetitive text until the completion-token limit is reached.

After rolling back the Docker image to v0.22.1, normal generation was restored, including correct arithmetic responses through the application.

This is a silent generation-quality failure rather than an initialization crash or API availability issue.

title: CPU KV offload crashes with Xid 31 on NVIDIA vGPU — cuMemcpyBatchAsync faults even with a single valid descriptor
body: Summary: - GPU: NVIDIA H200 NVL exposed to the guest as an SR-IOV **vGPU** (70 GiB profile), Proxmox VE host - vGPU manager (host): 595.91.04, guest driver: 595.91.07 - Reproduced on vLLM 0.31.0 (wheel) and on main @ `f8471164b` (precompiled), Python 3.14, torch 2.13.0, TP=1 With CPU KV offloading enabled (`OffloadingConnector`), the engine dies on the **first** batch of GPU→CPU stores with `CUDA error: unspecified launch failure`, and the host logs `NVRM: Xid 31` (GPU MMU fault) for every crash. We first hit it with Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 and Gemma 4 31B, but the root cause is model-independent: `cuMemcpyBatchAsync`, used by `ops.swap_blocks_batch`, faults on this vGPU even for a single in-bounds descriptor. Host side, one entry per run: A longer script ([swap_test.py](https://gist.github.com/jerry102039/860de1bb1810a962c58bab7668bd2a03)) moves random 4 MiB blocks in both directions between a GPU tensor and `cudaHostRegister`ed host memory, using vLLM's own descriptor buffers (`_new_descriptor_buffers`) and only in-bounds addresses: | Implementation (same descriptors, same addresses) | Result | |---|---| | `ops.swap_blocks_batch` (cuMemcpyBatchAsync), 64 descriptors/call, `/dev/shm`-backed host memory (as in `SharedOffloadRegion`) | ❌ launch failure + Xid 31 | | same, anonymous host memory | ❌ launch failure + Xid 31 | | same, **1 descriptor/call** | ❌ launch failure + Xid 31 | | one plain `cuMemcpyAsync` per descriptor | ✅ ~48 GiB/s both directions, 0 mismatches | So the addresses, the pinned host memory and the DMA path itself are fine; only the batched API faults. `VLLM_KV_OFFLOAD_MAX_BATCH_DESCRIPTORS=1` does not help for the same reason. `vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"OffloadingConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"cpu_bytes_to_use":68719476736}}'` crashes deterministically on the first offload store (same scheduler state and block IDs every run). With `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1`, all model kernels complete

title: DeepSeek-V4.1 crashes in decoder-replay CUDA graph with --moe-backend flashinfer_moe_ep_* (input_ids int32 vs int64)
body: - vLLM `main`: `flashinfer_moe_ep_mega_deep_gemm` reproduced on `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` arm64 `sha256:f853a683…` (built from 7d0b4e57aa); `flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl` reproduced on c41b2639e2 + #59912 + #59900, which that backend needs to start. Both include #59532. - DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (revision `2cba9e42`), 4× GB200, FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1, torch 2.13.0. DeepSeek-V4.1 served with a FlashInfer MegaMoE backend at TP=1 with DP+EP starts and answers short prompts, then crashes once it serves long prompts or batched prefills (here GSM8K 5-shot at `--max-concurrency 128`): On 4× GB200 at DEP=4, GSM8K (1319 questions, 5-shot) scores 0.027 with `flashinfer_moe_ep_mega_deep_gemm` (0.117 in an earlier run; the score depends on when the engine dies) and 0.070 with `flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl`, versus 0.899 for both with the fix. Once the engine dies, requests get HTTP 500 until the API server exits, then fail with connection errors. **Cause.** `DecoderReplayCudaGraphManager` sizes its `input_ids` buffer as int64 for every backend in `MEGA_MOE_BACKENDS` (`vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/decoder_replay_cudagraph.py:59-60`), which includes both `flashinfer_moe_ep_*` backends. `DeepseekV4Model.forward` casts `input_ids` to int64 only for `NATIVE_MEGA_MOE_BACKENDS` (`vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/model.py:929-930`), so the FlashInfer backends pass the runner's int32 ids and `index_select(out=)` rejects the mismatch. It doesn't show at startup or on short prompts because `run()` is only reached when a step is large enough to use a replay batch (a PIECEWISE step of at least 768 padded tokens, or an eager step with a prefill chunk over the 128-token window) and that batch dispatches to a replay CUDA graph; capture feeds the buffers directly and the eager fallback has no `out=`. By the code, a single prompt of 768 or more tokens is enough; GSM8K 5-shot at concurrency 128 reaches such steps right away. The two checks diverged when #54049 narrowed the model's cast to the native bac

title: DotsToolParser drops tool calls when request.tools is None and crashes on FunctionTool
body: In `vllm/tool_parsers/dots_tool_parser.py`, two issues affect tool call extraction: 1. **`self.tools` is ignored when `request.tools` is `None`:** When `DotsToolParser` is initialized with `tools` (e.g. `DotsToolParser(tokenizer, tools=[...])`), `extract_tool_calls` and `extract_tool_calls_streaming` only query `request.tools`. If `request.tools` is omitted or `None`, `_known_tool_names` is empty, causing all valid `<dots_function_call>` invocations to be silently dropped as normal text (`tools_called=False`, empty `tool_calls`). 2. **AttributeError with OpenAI Responses API (`FunctionTool`):** `_known_tool_names` and `_tool_schema` hardcode `tool.function.name` and `tool.function.parameters`. When tools are provided via the Responses API (`ResponsesRequest` with `FunctionTool`), `tool.function` does not exist (`FunctionTool` exposes `.name` and `.parameters` directly). This triggers an unhandled `AttributeError: 'FunctionTool' object has no attribute 'function'`, resulting in an unhandled 500 Internal Server Error in serving. > **Note:** I have already identified the root cause, implemented a clean fix utilizing `_extract_tool_info` from `vllm.tool_parsers.utils` and `self.tools` fallback, verified the fix with 13/13 passing regression tests, and will submit a PR linking to this issue immediately. 1. When `request.tools` is `None`, `DotsToolParser` should fall back to `self.tools`. 2. `DotsToolParser` should use `_extract_tool_info` to extract tool schemas and support both `ChatCompletionToolsParam` and `FunctionTool`.
label: bug

title: kv_cache_dtype="float16" on a bf16 model crashes the engine during CUDA-graph capture — RuntimeError: query and key must have the same dtype (flash_api.cpp:601)
body: For a **bfloat16** model (e.g. `Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct`, which defaults to bf16), setting `kv_cache_dtype="float16"` is **accepted at config-validation time**, but the engine crashes later — during CUDA-graph capture / attention warmup — with a raw CUDA kernel assertion: Root cause: the FLASH_ATTN backend passes the **bf16 query** and the **fp16 key/value cache** straight into `flash_attn_varlen_func` without casting the query to the KV-cache dtype. The `mha_varlen_fwd` kernel requires `query`/`key` to share a dtype, so it asserts. Note the FLASHINFER backend does **not** have this problem — its log shows it resolves/casts the query dtype to match the KV cache (`FlashInfer resolved query dtypes: prefill=torch.bfloat16 ... kv_cache_dtype=torch.float8_e4m3fn`), which is why the `fp8*` KV values all run fine. The crash is specific to the flash-attn path with a mismatched non-fp8 KV dtype. This is a missing cross-field validation / missing cast: `CacheConfig._validate_cache_dtype` (`vllm/config/cache.py`) only emits an `info` log and never checks compatibility between `cache_dtype` and the model `dtype`; the attention backend selector likewise validates `kv_cache_dtype` against hardware/backend support *in isolation*, without reconciling it with the model's query/key dtype. Either the engine works (cast the query to the KV-cache dtype, as the FLASHINFER path already does for `fp8`), or the incompatible combination is rejected cleanly at config-validation time with a descriptive error, e.g.: Currently the mismatch is only discovered mid-warmup as a raw CUDA assertion. Config accepted → engine loads weights → `profile_cudagraph_memory` → `capture_model` → `forward_fn(CUDAGraphMode.NONE)` → `unified_attention_with_output` → flash-attn `forward` → `torch.ops._vllm_fa2_C.varlen_fwd` → `RuntimeError`. - vLLM: 0.31.0 (official wheel) - PyTorch: 2.13.0+cu130 - GPU: NVIDIA RTX A6000 (sm86), CUDA 13.0 - OS: Linux 6.8.0-138-generic, Python 3.12.13 - Model: `Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-I

title: EPLB counts load for the wrong expert when step_interval < window_size
body: Any EPLB setup with eplb_config step_interval smaller than window_size. EPLB records load per physical slot. When step_interval < window_size only step_interval rows of the window are refreshed between two rearranges. The other rows still hold load recorded under the old map. The next rearrange reads them with the new map so that load is counted for whichever expert now sits in the slot. Small example with 2 experts, 2 slots, window_size=4 and step_interval=2. Expert 0 is hot and expert 1 is idle. After a rearrange that swaps them, the window holds two rows with load in slot 0 (old map) and two rows with load in slot 1 (new map). The next rearrange maps slot 0 to expert 1, so the idle expert looks as hot as expert 0. Async EPLB has the same problem per layer, since each layer switches to its new map in a later step. The defaults (window_size=1000, step_interval=3000) are not affected, because every rearrange starts from a fully refreshed window.
label: bug

title: Sparse MLA indexer's expanded_block_table_buffer is allocated after KV sizing (1 GiB at 1M context)
body: vLLM main @ 9367d8b969, B200, Model Runner V2, DSA models (sparse MLA indexer). The sparse MLA indexer's metadata builder allocates `expanded_block_table_buffer` (`vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/indexer.py`): Builders are constructed during KV cache initialization, after available memory has been profiled and the KV cache sized. So this buffer isn't accounted for and comes out of the activation headroom. It grows with both `max_num_batched_tokens` and `max_model_len`. With the default 16384 batched tokens and `max_model_len=1048576` (block size 64), it's 16384 × 16384 × 4 B = **1 GiB** per GPU. On 1×B200 (GLM-5.3-NVFP4 cut to 4 layers, `max_model_len=1048576`, `gpu_memory_utilization=0.97`), persistent allocations ended up about 1.9 GiB above the planned budget, with or without HiSparse; this buffer is the largest identified piece. A long prefill then OOMed when a 2.25 GiB MoE workspace allocation couldn't fit. The same config without HiSparse failed the same way at 0.975. Possible fixes: allocate it before memory profiling so it's counted, or size it to what the indexer actually needs. Decode token counts can in principle reach `max_num_batched_tokens`, so shrinking it needs care. Related: #60429 (same class of bug in HiSparse, a buffer allocated after KV sizing).
label: bug

title: --convert classify with --runner generate crashes engine startup with a bare AssertionError (pooler_config is not None)
body: The mutually-inconsistent combination `convert="classify"` (requires a pooling path) with `runner="generate"` is **not rejected at config-validation time**. The engine crashes later during model initialization with a bare assertion: This is a missing cross-field validation: `convert=classify` implies a pooler-capable model configuration, while `runner=generate` means no pooler config is ever constructed. The invalid combination survives `EngineArgs.create_engine_config()` and only fails deep inside model init as a raw `AssertionError` instead of a descriptive `ValueError`. A clean, descriptive rejection at config-validation time, e.g.: Config accepted → EngineCore startup → `initialize_model` → `_init_pooler` → `assert pooler_config is not None` → bare `AssertionError`, engine startup fails. - vLLM: 0.31.0 (official wheel) - PyTorch: 2.13.0+cu130 - GPU: NVIDIA RTX A6000 (sm86), CUDA 13.0 - OS: Linux 6.8.0-138-generic, Python 3.12.13 - Model: `Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct` - Found by a config-interaction test generator probing the (`convert` × `runner`) pair. - Related observation on the same version: `convert="embed"` with the default runner auto-selects a pooling model, so a plain generative probe (`LLM.generate`) is rejected with "LLM.generate() is only supported for generative models" — i.e., `convert` silently flips the effective runner; only the *explicit* mismatch (`classify` + `generate`) reaches the raw assert.
label: bug

title: moe_backend="batched_triton" crashes engine startup on unquantized MoE model — TypeError: BatchedTritonExperts.__init__() missing 2 required positional arguments
body: Selecting `moe_backend="batched_triton"` for an **unquantized** MoE model is accepted at config-validation time, but the engine crashes during model load with: The root cause is visible in `make_unquantized_moe_kernel` (`vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/oracle/unquantized.py`): when `prepare_finalize.activation_format != FusedMoEActivationFormat.BatchedExperts`, the else-branch constructs `experts_cls(moe_config=..., quant_config=...)` **without** `max_num_tokens` / `num_dispatchers` — but `BatchedTritonExperts.__init__` requires both. So whenever the MoE backend selector routes `BatchedTritonExperts` through the non-batched prepare/finalize path, startup crashes instead of either working or being cleanly rejected at config time. Two independent configurations produced the identical crash (same file/line): | variant | extra args | |---|---| | A | `enable_expert_parallel=True` | | B | `attention_backend="FLASH_ATTN_DIFFKV"` (no `enable_expert_parallel`) | Either `moe_backend="batched_triton"` works on an unquantized MoE model, or the incompatible combination is rejected cleanly at config-validation time (`ValueError` from `create_engine_config`). Currently the invalid routing is only discovered mid-model-load as a raw `TypeError`. Config accepted → EngineCore crashes during `process_weights_after_loading` → `make_unquantized_moe_kernel` → `BatchedTritonExperts(...)` raises `TypeError`. - vLLM: 0.31.0 (official wheel) - PyTorch: 2.13.0+cu130 - GPU: NVIDIA RTX A6000 (sm86), CUDA 13.0 - OS: Linux 6.8.0-138-generic, Python 3.12.13 - Model: `Qwen/Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B-Chat` (unquantized checkpoints) - Found by a config-interaction test generator: the pair (`enable_expert_parallel` × `moe_backend`) and (`attention_backend` × `moe_backend`) were probed with frontier (zero-incidence) enum values; `batched_triton` passed `EngineArgs.create_engine_config()` in both cases, so the invalid routing is not caught by any config-level guard. - The same model runs fine with the defaul

title: HiSparse: long prefill batched with decodes can OOM a running server
body: vLLM main @ ad0f67a7ec (re-confirmed on 12b005eefa), 1×B200, FlashInfer sparse MLA, fp8 KV, Model Runner V2. With HiSparse, a long prompt batched with running decodes can crash EngineCore with CUDA OOM, and the running requests die with it. This happens even when all of the prompt's KV is on GPU. In a mixed decode/prefill batch, the prefill rows don't read the GPU-resident pages directly. Instead: - the prefilling request's entire history is copied into a temporary GPU buffer on every layer (`stage_prefill_rows`), about 0.55 GiB at 1M tokens; - decode and prefill run as two kernels joined by `torch.cat`, about 1 GiB at 16K batched tokens. Neither allocation is needed when every page is GPU-resident, and startup profiling reserves neither. The cause is the `num_decode_tokens == 0 and all_context_pages_resident` condition: it was in the FlashInfer, FlashAttn and SM120 backends, and since #55866 it lives in the shared `SparseMLACommonImpl.forward_mqa`. FlashMLA sparse BF16 copies on every prefill. **Not a risk: prompts that spill to host** (e.g. a 1M-token prefill misrouted to a HiSparse decoder). The history copy is required there and unreserved, but it is capped by `max_model_len` (one layer at a time). On GLM-5.3-NVFP4 TP4 with the prompt forced to spill (util 0.90, 24 decodes), main completes with the per-step peak only 0.88 GiB over the profiled peak, well within headroom. #60424 tried to reserve it and was closed. The model is cut to 4 layers so a 1M-token prompt fits on one B200's GPU. Keep 2 requests decoding (512-token prompts), then send random-token prompts up to 1.04M with `max_tokens=1`. | config | 1.04M prompt | per-step peak over base at ~1M | |---|---|---| | no HiSparse, with decodes | OK | 4.91 GiB | | HiSparse, no decodes | OK | 4.91 GiB | | HiSparse, with decodes | **EngineCore OOM at 934K context** | 6.30 GiB | Related: #60429 removed a separate unaccounted buffer (per-layer prefill mirror staging). Tracking: #60072
label: bug

title: tool_choice="required"` streaming drops tool calls when one delta completes more than one call
body: With `tool_choice="required"` the model writes a JSON array of tool calls, and the serving layer streams it through `extract_required_tool_call_streaming` (`vllm/tool_parsers/streaming.py`). The helper looks only at the last object of the partially parsed array (`obj[-1]`) and returns at most one tool call per delta. When a delta completes more than one call, the earlier calls are never streamed: The non-streaming path returns both calls for the same text. Streamed one character at a time, both calls arrive, so the result depends on how the text is cut. Deltas of several tokens are what `--stream-interval` above 1 produces. Every call of the array is streamed with its name and its arguments, whatever the size of the deltas. The helper would need to go over every object of the array that still has something unsent, with the "name sent" state kept per index instead of in one boolean.
label: bug

title: FP8 KV cache startup can OOM because CUDA graph memory is omitted from the cache budget
body: On a 24 GiB GPU, `LLM(..., kv_cache_dtype="fp8")` is accepted but fails during startup with an out-of-memory error, while the identical engine using the default KV cache dtype answers successfully. Observed failure: The startup accounting allocates about 19.93 GiB to the KV cache after subtracting a near-zero CUDA graph estimate. CUDA graph capture happens afterwards and consumes about 0.80 GiB in the FP8 case, pushing actual usage beyond the memory reserved by `gpu_memory_utilization`. Reducing `gpu_memory_utilization` avoids the failure. KV cache sizing should reserve the actual CUDA graph memory so an accepted configuration does not exceed its memory budget during graph capture or the first sampling allocation. If vLLM cannot fit the configuration, it should fail early with an actionable error. Make `profile_cudagraph_memory()` account for the actual graph capture cost, including its dependence on the number of KV blocks, or adjust the KV cache after graph capture when measured use exceeds the requested budget.
label: bug

title: `LLM.generate()` never returns when `max_num_scheduled_tokens=0`
body: `SchedulerConfig.max_num_scheduled_tokens` uses a lower bound of `ge=0`, so vLLM accepts zero as a valid scheduling budget. The engine then has no tokens available to schedule: initialization succeeds, but `generate()` makes no progress and never returns or reports an error. vLLM should reject `max_num_scheduled_tokens=0` during configuration with a clear `ValueError`. An accepted configuration should not cause an unbounded silent hang. Require `max_num_scheduled_tokens` to be greater than zero and apply the existing non-positive-budget validation regardless of whether speculative decoding is enabled.
label: bug

title: InternLM2 streaming tool parser drops characters from function arguments
body: `Internlm2ToolParser.extract_tool_calls_streaming` can emit argument deltas whose concatenation is not the final function arguments. Characters are silently dropped as the partially parsed JSON grows. Once the emitted text is no longer a prefix of the completed arguments, `get_remaining_unstreamed_args()` cannot flush the missing tail. The attached `repro.py` feeds the same call using two chunk boundaries. For the failing split, it prints: instead of: The concatenated streaming argument deltas should exactly equal the completed tool call arguments for every valid chunk boundary. Stream slices from the raw argument text while tracking the number of characters already emitted. Avoid reconstructing deltas from repeatedly serialized partial JSON, which can introduce temporary suffixes that later disappear.
label: bug

title: `TensorizerConfig(lora_dir=...)` leaves `tensorizer_dir=None` and breaks serialization round trips
body: `TensorizerConfig.__post_init__` derives `tensorizer_dir` only when `tensorizer_uri` is supplied explicitly. A configuration created using the documented LoRA-only form keeps `tensorizer_dir=None`. Code that writes the adapter then constructs a path such as `None/adapter_config.json`, and serializing and rebuilding the configuration changes its value. A `lora_dir`-only configuration should resolve `tensorizer_dir` consistently, and `TensorizerConfig(**config.to_serializable())` should be equivalent to the original configuration. Derive `tensorizer_dir` from the resolved `tensorizer_uri` in all cases, including when that URI was inferred from `lora_dir`.
label: bug

title: `append_replayssm_ring` asserts for supported non-divisible Mamba group counts
body: `MambaStateShapeCalculator.mamba2_state_shape` supports `n_groups` values that are not divisible by the tensor-parallel world size by extending the groups assigned to head shards. Passing the resulting state shape to `append_replayssm_ring`, however, calls `divide(n_groups, tp_world_size)` on the original group count and raises an assertion. This raises: `append_replayssm_ring` should use the same group-extension rule as `mamba2_state_shape`, so a state shape accepted by the calculator can have a ReplaySSM ring appended without an assertion. Extend `n_groups` for the tensor-parallel head shards before dividing it, matching the logic already used by `mamba2_state_shape`.
label: bug

title: `validate_regex_is_buildable` (outlines backend) misses `\b` and backreferences inside groups
body: `vllm.v1.structured_output.backend_outlines.validate_regex_is_buildable` rejects regex features that `outlines_core` cannot build (word boundaries, backreferences, look-arounds), but its helper `_check_unsupported` recurses only into `BRANCH` and `MAX_REPEAT` nodes, not into `SUBPATTERN` (group) nodes. The same feature wrapped in a group passes validation: `outlines_core.Index` fails for both accepted patterns (`Failed to build DFA`), so such a request is admitted and fails later in the engine core (`StructuredOutputManager._create_grammar` logs a traceback) instead of being rejected with a validation error. Recursing into `SUBPATTERN` (`tval[3]`), as `_prefix_needs_context` in the same file already does, fixes it. Patterns with an unsupported feature are rejected wherever the feature appears.
label: bug

title: xLAM tool parser (streaming) drops arguments nested deeper than two levels and truncates at a `}` inside a string
body: `xLAMToolParser.extract_tool_calls_streaming` extracts each call's `arguments` object with a regular expression that allows only one inner level of braces and ignores string literals. Arguments nested three levels deep stream as an empty string, and a `}` inside a string value ends the arguments early; `extract_tool_calls` (non-streaming) handles both: The streamed arguments equal the non-streaming ones.
label: bug

title: DeepSeek-V3 tool parser returns no tool calls when the JSON arguments span several lines
body: `DeepSeekV3ToolParser`'s regexes match the body of the json python import json from vllm.entrypoints.openai.chat_completion.protocol import ChatCompletionRequest from vllm.tool_parsers.deepseekv3_tool_parser import DeepSeekV3ToolParser class Tok: def get_vocab(self): return {"<｜tool▁calls▁begin｜>": 0, "<｜tool▁calls▁end｜>": 1, "<｜tool▁call▁begin｜>": 2, "<｜tool▁call▁end｜>": 3, "<｜tool▁sep｜>": 4} args = json.dumps({"city": "Tokyo"}, indent=2) out = ("<｜tool▁calls▁begin｜><｜tool▁call▁begin｜>function<｜tool▁sep｜>get_weather\n" f" <｜tool▁call▁end｜><｜tool▁calls▁end｜>") print(DeepSeekV3ToolParser(Tok()).extract_tool_calls(out, ChatCompletionRequest(messages=[], model="m"))) ``` One call `get_weather` with `{"city": "Tokyo"}`, whatever the whitespace inside the JSON block.
label: bug

title: InternLM2 tool parser (streaming) drops all content after `<|action_start|>` when no `<|plugin|>` follows
body: `Internlm2ToolParser.extract_tool_calls_streaming` stops emitting content once `<|action_start|>` appears and waits for `<|action_start|><|plugin|>`. When the action is not a plugin call (InternLM2 also emits `<|interpreter|>` blocks), or the generation ends right after `<|action_start|>`, the rest of the output is never streamed. The non-streaming `extract_tool_calls` returns the same text verbatim as content. Streaming returns the same content as non-streaming: text after `<|action_start|>` that does not turn out to be a plugin call is released as content (at the latest when the stream ends).
label: bug

title: Olmo3 reasoning parser drops the final streamed delta when it is a substring of `<think>`/`</think>` (e.g. "think")
body: In streaming mode, `Olmo3ReasoningBuffer.add_text` holds a delta back when `string_overlap(delta_text, marker)` reports an overlap with `<think>` or `</think>`. `string_overlap` also reports *containment*, so a delta that merely occurs inside a marker (`think`, `in`, `k`, `>`, `/`, ...) is buffered as if it could start a marker. If the generation ends on such a delta, the buffered text is never emitted: nothing flushes the buffer at the end of the stream. Non-streaming `extract_reasoning` returns the full content. Last deltas `>` (after `<div`) and `in` + `k` behave the same way. The attached `repro.py` exits 1 while the problem is present. Streaming and non-streaming give the same content; a delta is held back only while it can still be the *start* of a marker (a suffix of the text that is a prefix of the marker), and held text is flushed when the stream ends.
label: bug

title: LoRA adapters using PEFT features vLLM does not implement load without error and give wrong outputs
body: `PEFTHelper.from_dict` (`vllm/lora/peft_helper.py`) keeps only the `adapter_config.json` keys it knows and drops the rest, and `_validate_features` only rejects DoRA and unsupported `modules_to_save`. So an adapter that relies on a PEFT feature vLLM doesn't implement loads without any error or warning and is served with wrong outputs. This is the same class of problem as #59799 (`rank_pattern` / `alpha_pattern`), for other fields. Repro on main (0872ddf4b9), tiny random Llama, PEFT 0.21.2, RTX 3090. Each adapter is saved with PEFT and reloaded with `PeftModel.from_pretrained` for the reference (`VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0` only because this machine has no `nvcc`): Output: The plain adapter matches PEFT within bf16 noise; the others don't, and nothing in the log mentions the dropped fields. What goes wrong for each field: - `lora_bias=True`: PEFT saves a `lora_B.bias` tensor. Since #53555 (which allowed `.bias` for the `score` / `classifier` heads of classification adapters), `parse_fine_tuned_lora_name` also accepts `lora_A.bias` / `lora_B.bias` and maps them to the same module as the weight, so whichever tensor is loaded last becomes `lora_b`. With safetensors the bias comes first in key order, so lora_B's weight survives and the bias is dropped; with a `.bin` adapter the ordering can differ and lora_B can end up as the 1-D bias. Before #53555, such adapters were rejected with `... is unsupported LoRA weight`. #53555 is in v0.31.0 but not in v0.30.0, so this is a regression in the v0.31.0 release. - `init_lora_weights` = `"pissa"` / `"pissa_niter_*"` / `"olora"` / `"corda"` / `"loftq"` / `"lora_ga"`: when PEFT loads such an adapter it rewrites the base layer weights (for example `pissa_init` and `corda_init` in `peft/tuners/lora/layer.py` assign `get_base_layer().weight.data`), so the adapter is only correct on the modified base. vLLM serves it on the unmodified base. PEFT's own `path_initial_model_for_weight_conversion` produces a regular adapter and resets the

body: - vLLM `0.30.0+g87ecf7d`, plus open PRs #56836 and #57139 and some local P2P hardening patches (see the note below). - torch 2.13.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0, `nixl-cu13` 1.3.2 (UCX backend). - 8× H100 80GB HBM3 per node, driver 580.126.20, RoCE. - Model: GLM-5.3, disaggregated prefill/decode. Prefill is DP4 × PCP8, one DP rank per node, with `TieringOffloadingSpec`: a 512 GiB CPU primary tier plus a `p2p` secondary tier over UCX. The code path below is unchanged on `main` (checked against `e11962fc1c`): our build's `session/server.py` is byte-identical to `main`, and `data/nixl.py`'s `write_blocks` is identical too. When the source side of a P2P fetch calls `NixlTransport.write_blocks` and NIXL raises (we saw `nixlRemoteDisconnectError` and `nixlNotFoundError`), the exception escapes to the session's message dispatcher, which only logs it. The requesting peer is never told the fetch failed. It waits for its round timeout (30 s here), aborts, and only then falls back to recomputing the prefix. Call chain, from our traceback (line numbers from our build, same code on `main`): `_submit_transfer` already has a fail-fast path, but only for `write_blocks` *returning* `None` (no remote descriptor list for the peer). That path marks the round finishing and calls `_finalize_outbound(kv_request_id, round_key, success=False)` so that "the peer and the local store jobs don't wait for finish_request or for `_STORE_TIMEOUT_S` / `_LOAD_TIMEOUT_S`". Nothing finalizes the round. title: `vllm preload` daemon never matches a dense (non-MoE) engine with `--data-parallel-size > 1` (WeightCacheKey `dp_size` mismatch)
body: With a dense (non-MoE) model and `--data-parallel-size N` (N > 1), engines started with `--load-format ipc_cache` never use the daemon started by `vllm preload` with the same flags. The daemon fingerprints each rank with `dp_size=N, dp_rank=r`, but a dense engine fingerprints every rank with `dp_size=1, dp_rank=0`, so the `WeightCacheKey` check fails on every rank. - With the default `fallback=true`, each rank logs one warning and loads from disk. The server works, but Fast Start does nothing, and the daemon keeps holding its own copy of the weights on every GPU. - With `"fallback": false`, the engine fails to start. The preload docs list data parallelism as supported ([`docs/features/preload.md` L26-L28](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/5f30fc7031cae49bf51073fc953d419b08f8887c/docs/features/preload.md#L26-L28), [L167](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/5f30fc7031cae49bf51073fc953d419b08f8887c/docs/features/preload.md#L167)) and do not restrict it to MoE models. Two GPUs, public dense model. Wait for `Weight cache daemon READY`, then: `--enforce-eager`, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.2` and `--max-model-len 2048` only keep the run small because the GPUs on my machine are shared. With the default `fallback=true`, the server starts and answers, but no rank logs `Mapped ... tensors from the weight cache daemon`. Instead: The daemon logs the same two mismatches and keeps serving. With `--model-loader-extra-config '{"fallback": false}'` added to `vllm serve`, `EngineCore failed to start`. Rank 0 raises `CacheConfigMismatchError: WeightCacheKey mismatch on fields: ['dp_size']`, rank 1 the same with `['dp_size', 'dp_rank']`. Two controls on the same machine: - The same commands without `--data-parallel-size` on one GPU: the engine logs `Mapped 339 tensors from the weight cache daemon (zero_copy mode)`. - One `vllm preload` **without** `--data-parallel-size` per GPU (`CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0` and `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1`), then the same `vllm serve ... --data-pa

title: Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 (TP4, MI355X) accuracy collapses at high concurrency with `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`; fine with AITER off
body: With AITER enabled, Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 at TP=4 on MI355X gives correct outputs at low concurrency. At ≥128 concurrent requests, outputs get much worse (GSM8K, greedy decoding): - GSM8K accuracy drops from 96% to about 64%. - Many responses end after ≤5 tokens. - Many other responses run much longer than usual. Setting `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=0` (everything else unchanged) brings accuracy at c256 back to 96.7%. The bug is not caused by: - the attention backend; - the model runner (V1 or V2); - prefix caching; - the AITER FP8 linear kernel. Some AITER component other than those is involved. Custom all-reduce and RMSNorm were not tested separately (see "Not yet tested"). Greedy outputs should not depend on how many other requests share the batch. The defaults that apply are: - max_num_seqs 256; - max_num_batched_tokens 16384; - cudagraph_mode FULL_AND_PIECEWISE, capture sizes up to 512. The log shows: - `Using V2 Model Runner` - `GDN decode kernel: triton` - all-reduce backends `['AITER_CUSTOM', 'PYNCCL']` - `fuse_allreduce_rms: True` - GPU KV cache of about 15.4M tokens (usage stays below 7%). The eval runs GSM8K test (all 1319 questions) through `/v1/chat/completions` with these settings: - temperature 0, max_tokens 8192. - Prompt: `"Solve the following math problem. Put the final answer, a number only, on the last line in the form 'Answer: <number>'.\n\n{question}"` - Client-side concurrency is controlled by an asyncio semaphore, and the client does not cap connections (`aiohttp.TCPConnector(limit=0)`). - The server log confirms that `Running:` reaches the target concurrency. All runs use a fresh server, one change at a time, and the full 1319 questions. | Config | Concurrency | Accuracy | Truncated (8192) | Mean completion tokens | Wrong w/ no parsable answer | Responses ≤5 tokens | Error rate: first 256 reqs / rest | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | baseline (prefix caching on) | 64 | **96.1%** | 15 | 457 | 24 | 9 | 4% / 4% | | baseline | 128 | **90.7%** | 24 | 538 |
label: bug

title: GLM-5.3 TP8 on B200: illegal memory access when admitting a new request wave
body: - vLLM `528772a4bf` (main, 2026-10-05), torch 2.13.0+cu130, flashinfer-python 0.7.0.post1 - 8× NVIDIA B200, driver 595.91.07 - Model `RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-NVFP4`, TP8, FlashInfer sparse MLA, default `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` CUDA graphs, MRv2 With HiSparse enabled, the server crashes when a new wave of requests is admitted after an earlier wave has finished on the same server. Every GPU-memory-related error surfaces inside HiSparse's residency resolution during piecewise-graph replay (or as a segfault in `cudaGraphLaunch`). title: `/inference/v1/generate` doesn't pass `reasoning_ended` or `reasoning_parser_kwargs`, so structured outputs start later than on `/v1/chat/completions`
body: Chat tells the engine when to start enforcing structured outputs. The scale-out generate path doesn't, so the same rendered request can be constrained differently depending on which path serves it. `OpenAIServingChat` passes two things to `engine_client.generate` (`vllm/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/serving.py`): - `reasoning_ended=True` when `include_reasoning=false` or when the Mistral grammar came from the parser (`request._grammar_from_parser`). Otherwise it checks the prompt with the parser. - `reasoning_parser_kwargs={"chat_template_kwargs": ...}`, so the engine's reasoner knows about things like `enable_thinking`. `/inference/v1/generate` passes neither (`vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/serving.py`), and `GenerateRequest` has no fields for them. With `--reasoning-parser` set, the engine then defaults to `reasoning_ended=None`. It checks the prompt and if reasoning hasn't ended there it holds the grammar until the model ends reasoning (`vllm/v1/structured_output/__init__.py`). Its reasoner is also built without the template kwargs. What that means in practice: - **`include_reasoning=false`**: chat constrains from the first token. Generate lets the model reason unconstrained first. - **Mistral grammar** (tool choice `required` / named, JSON): the grammar has its own optional `think?` rule and expects to start at token 0. On generate it only starts after `[/THINK]`, so if the model doesn't think, the constraint is never applied. - **Reasoners that read `chat_template_kwargs`**: the engine side reasoner can disagree with the frontend about whether thinking is on. #39130 looks like the same thing on the full path (Gemma4, `enable_thinking=false`) and generate never gets the kwargs. This affects any client of the render → generate path, including the new `output_mode="text"` from #58588. Suggested fix: have `/render` work out `reasoning_ended` and `reasoning_parser_kwargs` the same way main chat does, carry them on `GenerateRequest` and pass them
label: bug

body: - vLLM `main` at `f590eb2448a51028f6044c6f60104ce0ef3189e9`, torch 2.13.0+cu130 - NVIDIA GB300 (SM 10.3), driver 580.167.08, CUDA toolkit 13.1 - Models: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat` (TP=1) and `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.1` (TP=4) - Attention backend: `TRITON_MLA`, `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` With `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, the output of an MLA model changes when its prefill is split into chunks. Both DeepSeek models above fail the chunked-prefill test of the batch-invariance suite, while their needle tests and `bs1_vs_bsN` bitwise tests pass. Both are on the tested-models list in `docs/features/batch_invariance.md`. **Repro** Three runs in fresh processes give the same failure and the same delta. `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.1` fails the same test the same way. **Isolation** The difference does not need other requests in the batch. title: CPU attention rejects DiffusionGemma int32 causal mask since #51994
body: Since #51994, DiffusionGemma fails on the CPU backend at engine startup with: Changes in the PR made DiffusionGemma's per-request causal mask `int32`, and updated FlashAttention and Triton to read it: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/7867d6c52d4542c1b5da641f8ca79124be497ee3/vllm/model_executor/models/diffusion_gemma.py#L916-L918 CPU attention passes the same mask to its C++ ops, which still read it as `bool`: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/7867d6c52d4542c1b5da641f8ca79124be497ee3/csrc/cpu/cpu_attn.cpp#L81-L82 The CPU tests build their own `bool` mask. CPU CI stayed green. https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/7867d6c52d4542c1b5da641f8ca79124be497ee3/tests/kernels/attention/test_cpu_attn.py#L475 On a CPU build of `main`: Any DiffusionGemma request on CPU fails the same way at startup. title: NIXL pull: one wedged connection repeatedly strands decode KV blocks (production log analysis)
body: - Production: disaggregated P/D on a build based on v0.30.0, `nixl==1.4.1`, `NixlConnector` in pull mode, `kv_load_failure_policy: fail`, default `engine_ttl=3600`, mlx5 `rc` transport. - Decode is TP2. Prefill is TP8/DCP8, so each decode request posts 16 READs (2 decode workers x 8 prefill ranks). About 40 prefill engines. - The connector's NIXL agent is created without `sync_mode` (see #59870). One decode engine leaked KV blocks in a staircase until it sat at ~97% utilization and stopped admitting anything but small requests. The decode pod's log shows the cause is **a single wedged connection**: one decode TP worker has a connection to one rank of one prefill engine on which no READ ever completes. Every request prefilled on that engine and routed to this decode engine loses the same READ, waits until the client gives up, is aborted, and leaves its blocks pinned. This is the production case behind #59872. That issue describes what vLLM does once a READ stays in `PROC`. This issue adds what the log shows about how it gets there and why it repeats. Stats lines normally report successful transfers in multiples of 16. Each episode starts with one that is one short, followed by ~45 minutes with no engine activity, after which the KV floor has risen: | Stuck at (UTC) | Transfers in that line | Silence after | KV floor after | |---|---|---|---| | 08:08:38 | 15 | 45m00s | 5.5% | | 09:16:38 | 15 | 45m10s | 8.6% | | 12:24:18 | 15 | 45m21s | 30.9% | | 13:14:39 | 15 | 45m30s | 36.3% | | 14:22:29 | 31 | 45m10s | 38.9% | | 15:38:39 | 31 | 44m50s | 63.1% | | 16:28:59 | 15 | 45m10s | 65.2% | | 17:19:39 | 31 | 45m00s | 67.0% | | 18:16:39 | 15 | 45m00s | 76.3% | | 19:28:29 | 31 | 21m20s | 95.3% | `Num failed transfers` stays 0 and nothing is logged. The ~2,700 s wait matches an upstream timeout; the request is aborted at that point (inferred, the log has no abort line). While it waits, the engine receives no other traffic. - **Only one of four engines in the pod is affected.** Sam

title: NIXL: `remove_remote_agent` does not release UCX endpoints, so each `engine_ttl` eviction + re-handshake leaks until handshakes fail
body: - vLLM `main` at `54020c3c3e`, `nixl==1.4.1` (`nixl-cu13` wheel, bundled UCX), Python 3.12. - Repro box: 8x H100, no RDMA NIC, so UCX uses `tcp` / `cuda_ipc` / `sm`. - Production deployment this came from: disaggregated P/D, `NixlConnector` (pull), decode TP2, each decode worker loads 8 remote agents per prefill engine, mlx5 `rc` transport, default `engine_ttl=3600`. `nixl_agent.remove_remote_agent()` (`invalidateRemoteMD`) returns success but does not destroy the UCX endpoints created by `add_remote_agent()` (`loadRemoteMD`). vLLM calls it for every agent in `_cleanup_remote_engine` (`nixl/base_worker.py:3525`) and assumes the transport resources come back. They do not, so every `engine_ttl` eviction followed by a re-handshake permanently leaks one UCX endpoint per UCX worker per remote rank in the decode worker process. **Production symptom.** After ~2,290 `add_remote_agent` calls (and ~280 evictions that had already removed ~2,250 of those agents), two decode workers hit a fixed ceiling two hours apart and every later handshake failed: That is consistent with per-QP DEVX buffers never being freed until the process reaches `vm.max_map_count`. Evictions after the wall freed nothing. The least-loaded decode rank failed first because idle pairings are the ones that get evicted and re-handshaken. **Standalone reproducer (no vLLM, no RDMA).** Two NIXL agents, UCX backend, `num_threads=4` as vLLM configures it. title: CPU async output snapshots can alias reused sampler buffers
body: Identified while working on https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59107. With async scheduling, the V2 model runner snapshots each step's sampled tokens and counts with `async_copy_to_np()`. It reads the snapshot after the next step has started. https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/e006d761a526d0a69555a59f7c10c0c889babd98/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/async_utils.py#L264-L265 On GPU, `.to("cpu", non_blocking=True)` copies into new memory. On CPU the tensor is already on the target device. PyTorch returns the same tensor and `.numpy()` shares its memory. If the buffer is reused, the next step overwrites the snapshot before it is read. DiffusionGemma reuses its sampled-token buffers on every step: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/e006d761a526d0a69555a59f7c10c0c889babd98/vllm/model_executor/models/diffusion_gemma.py#L1203-L1213 The CPU platform forces sync scheduling for every model, and sync reads each output before the next step runs: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/e006d761a526d0a69555a59f7c10c0c889babd98/vllm/platforms/cpu.py#L312-L314 It appears as soon as async scheduling is enabled on CPU. I enabled it for DiffusionGemma only, with a local change to that hook, to test structured reads. No model is needed. This runs on any CPU build: we get: The expected output is `[[0], [0]] [0, 0]`. A snapshot should not change after it is taken. I sent the same seeded read 10 times with a batch of 1 and 10 times with a batch of 4. The read uses a 32-token canvas on a 64-token server, is read-only and runs one step. With async scheduling, every output is corrupted: I logged each snapshot when it was taken and again when it was read. Two steps are overwritten: - The prefill snapshot has no tokens. It picks up the read step's count and first token, and returns a phantom token. - The read's own snapshot is overwritten by the next in-flight step. - The phantom token counts toward the read's 32-token limit. The read keeps 31 of its own positions and returns 31 logpr
label: bug

title: LoRA adapters with PEFT rank_pattern / alpha_pattern are served with the wrong scaling
body: `PEFTHelper` (`vllm/lora/peft_helper.py`) reads `r` and `lora_alpha` from `adapter_config.json` and applies one scaling, `lora_alpha / r`, to every LoRA module. PEFT also supports per-module rank and alpha through `rank_pattern` and `alpha_pattern`, and scales each module by its own `alpha_m / r_m`. vLLM ignores both fields, so every module whose pattern changes `alpha_m / r_m` is served with the wrong scaling. Nothing warns about it: `_validate_features` rejects DoRA and unsupported `modules_to_save`, but patterns are accepted and dropped. The relevant code is unchanged on main (0979892992). This matters most for MoE. PEFT's LoRA docs recommend `target_parameters` on the experts with `rank_pattern={"experts.gate_up_proj": r // num_experts, ...}` and point to vLLM for serving. The experts are then scaled `r / (r // num_experts)` times more in PEFT than in vLLM. With OLMoE-1B-7B (64 experts, `r=16`), a LoRA trained that way for 200 steps on wikitext-2 gives a held-out perplexity of 10.06 in PEFT and 11.28 in vLLM (base model: 13.09 / 13.08), so vLLM loses about 40% of the adapter's gain. Folding each module's scaling into `lora_B` and removing the patterns makes vLLM match PEFT again (10.06). Minimal repro with a tiny random dense model (vLLM 0.30.0, PEFT 0.21.2, RTX 3090; I set `VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0` only because this machine has no `nvcc`): Output: The folded adapter matches PEFT within bf16 noise; the original one doesn't. For MoE models that are not flagged `is_3d_moe_weight` (Qwen3-MoE, OLMoE, Mixtral, ...), a PEFT adapter that uses `target_parameters` on the experts kills the engine with a bare assertion. It works when the engine is started with `enable_mixed_moe_lora_format=True` and the request sets `is_3d_lora_weight=True`, but the error gives no hint of that: With `python repro.py mixed` it loads and generates. 1. Support the patterns: compute the scaling per module when the adapter is loaded, using PEFT's key matching (a pattern key matches a modu

title: deepseek_r1 streaming reasoning deltas are not detokenized (byte-level BPE glyphs)
body: With `--reasoning-parser deepseek_r1` and `"stream": true`, the reasoning deltas are emitted as raw byte-level BPE token glyphs instead of decoded UTF-8. `delta.content` is correct, and the corruption only shows up on non-ASCII output (CJK). Non-streaming is fine. Deployed via Docker, vLLM 0.21.0: vllm serve /models/deepseek \ --served-model-name DeepSeek-R1-0528-Qwen3-8B \ --dtype bfloat16 --tensor-parallel-size 1 --max-model-len 8192 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 --reasoning-parser deepseek_r1 \ --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 curl -N http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"DeepSeek-R1-0528-Qwen3-8B","messages":[{"role":"user", "content":"请用三句话介绍一下你自己。"}],"temperature":0.6, "max_tokens":256,"stream":true}' data: {...,"choices":[{"delta":{"reasoning":"Ċ"},...}]} data: {...,"choices":[{"delta":{"reasoning":"åĹ¯"},...}]} data: {...,"choices":[{"delta":{"reasoning":"ï¼Į"},...}]} first delta should be a newline, then "嗯", then "，" Byte-level analysis of the leaked glyphs: "Ċ" -> 0x0A -> "\n" "åĹ¯" -> E5 97 AF -> "嗯" "ï¼Į" -> EF BC 8C -> "，" i.e. the reasoning path looks like it returns convert_ids_to_tokens() output without the convert_tokens_to_string()/decode() step, and multi-byte characters also stay split across chunks at token boundaries. Control experiment: removing --reasoning-parser deepseek_r1 makes the same output arrive correctly (as regular content), and stream=false is also correct — so the issue is specific to the streaming reasoning path.

title: CUTLASS fp8 MoE corrupts valid tokens when CUDA-graph padding routes are `-1` (wrong `expert_first_token_offset` from `moe_permute`)
body: - vLLM **0.29.0** (tag), **0.30.0** (`ced6857afa0e`) and **`main` at `47de9d4d04`** (2026-10-01, precompiled kernels), identical results. - torch 2.13.0+cu130, H100 80GB HBM3 (SM 9.0), TP=1 and TP=2. - V2 model runner, default compilation (`VLLM_COMPILE`, `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` CUDA graphs), `VLLM_MOE_SKIP_PADDING=1` (default). - MoE backend auto-selected as `VLLM_CUTLASS` (`CutlassExpertsFp8`) for a compressed-tensors `FP8_DYNAMIC` checkpoint (per-channel weight scales, per-token dynamic activation scales). With the CUTLASS fp8 MoE backend, **valid tokens get the wrong MoE output whenever the batch contains padding tokens**. CUDA-graph replay pads small batches up to a capture size, and with `VLLM_MOE_SKIP_PADDING=1` the router writes `topk_ids = -1` for those padding tokens. The CUTLASS path then computes wrong per-expert offsets and runs some real tokens through the wrong expert's weights. User-visible effect (a 128-expert, top-4, fp8 MoE model): with single-request serving the first generated token often collapses (e.g. bf16 `'Yes'` p=0.90 becomes `'\n'` p=0.997 in fp8), and sampled output drifts into unrelated text. The same checkpoint is correct with batched requests, with `--moe-backend triton` or `marlin`, with `--enforce-eager`, with CUDA graphs disabled, or with `VLLM_MOE_SKIP_PADDING=0`. 56-expert and 224-expert fp8 models served the same way are also affected, less often. Output (identical on 0.29.0, 0.30.0 and `main`): Every padded batch size is wrong; the 6 correct sizes are the multiples of 8, which have no padding. When padding outnumbers the valid tokens (e.g. `n_valid=1, n_pad=7`), every offset equals the total route count, so every expert segment is empty and the valid tokens' MoE output is silently zero. Rows `[0, n)` of the CUTLASS MoE output, compared with the same call on the valid rows alone (relative error), for `n = 1..48` padded to the next vLLM CUDA-graph capture size (1, 2, 4, then multiples of 8): | padding rows | routing | valid-row erro

title: cudagraph_mode=FULL crashes on prefill with FlashInfer sparse MLA on SM100
body: vLLM main @ `2a52715ef7`, 1× B200 (SM100), Model Runner V2 (`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`). With `cudagraph_mode=FULL` and the FlashInfer sparse MLA backend on SM100 (`FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE`), the engine crashes as soon as a prefill chunk replays a FULL CUDA graph. `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`, the default, works. `FlashInferMLASparseTRTLLMMetadataBuilder` declares `AttentionCGSupport.ALWAYS` (added in #52783), so `FULL` mode captures FULL graphs for mixed/prefill batches too. Neither MLA prefill backend can replay those: | MLA prefill backend | Result | |---|---| | FlashAttention (default for DeepSeek-V3.2) | `CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered` during FULL-graph replay | | TRTLLM ragged (default for larger MLA dims, e.g. GLM-5.3) | `ValueError: TRTLLM ragged prefill contains mixed active and empty query rows: query_lens=[512, 0, 0, 0]`: the FULL graph pads the batch with empty requests | | FlashInfer | not valid for these MLA dimensions | In both failing cases, a 512-token prefill chunk is dispatched to a request-padded FULL graph. The variable-length verification FULL graphs that adaptive DSpark (#52783) needs may be what `ALWAYS` was meant for. If so, a lower support level plus the varlen-decode hook might cover that without capturing prefill. **Repro** (DeepSeek-V3.2 shrunk to 4 layers, dummy weights; no HiSparse or KV connector). Pass `TRTLLM_RAGGED` or `FLASH_ATTN` as the argument to pick the prefill backend: With `"cudagraph_mode": "FULL_AND_PIECEWISE"` the same script prints `OK 16`. This also blocks HiSparse users on `cudagraph_mode=FULL`. HiSparse has a separate hazard here: its prefill path branches on per-step page residency, which a FULL graph would freeze at capture. It is masked by this crash. AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to reproduce and write up this issue.
label: bug

title: Qwen2 key bias may degrade int4_per_token_head KV-cache accuracy
body: This issue was filed prematurely. **No real vLLM run on an NVIDIA GPU has confirmed degraded Qwen2 output.** I am closing it pending that check. - vLLM's int4 Triton kernels were run through Triton's CPU interpreter on Qwen-like keys. Attention error was 1.36 with the current path and 0.12 with the proposed correction; 0.12 is comparable to the no-bias case. - A CPU emulator matched those kernel results within 0.000003. The previously posted perplexity figures (13.80/137.6/14.26 for Qwen2.5-0.5B and 9.55/7,381/9.70 for Qwen2.5-1.5B) came from that emulation, **not from a GPU vLLM run**. Two emulator variants differed on the unpatched result. - Real Qwen2.5 key-projection bias magnitudes reach roughly 400. The suspected mechanism is that a per-token-head 4-bit scale is dominated by that constant and loses the smaller key variation. Run unpatched vLLM with Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct on an NVIDIA GPU using TRITON_ATTN and `--kv-cache-dtype int4_per_token_head`; compare its output with the same model using the default KV-cache dtype. Then run the proposed fix on that same setup. Record the environment, commands, output/quality results, and latency. The proposed correction removes key bias before cache quantization and restores its RoPE-dependent contribution in attention scores. Qwen2-VL, Qwen2.5-VL, and Qwen2-MoE are outside its scope. AI assistance was used in this investigation.
label: bug

title: Fast Start WeightCacheKey hashes only safetensors headers, so an ipc_cache engine can silently map another checkpoint's weights
body: `hash_checkpoint()` builds the `checkpoint` field of `WeightCacheKey` from each shard's file name and safetensors header only ([`protocol.py#L239-L272`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/863475eb9cd78ae6a4a22f1b90df7fe85e0af438/vllm/model_executor/model_loader/weight_cache/protocol.py#L239-L272)). The header holds tensor names, dtypes, shapes and offsets, but no weight values. Two local checkpoints with the same architecture and file layout (a base model and its fine-tune, `step_0` and `step_100`) therefore get the same key. If a daemon preloaded from checkpoint A is still running and an engine starts on checkpoint B with `--load-format ipc_cache`, the daemon's check ([`daemon.py#L399-L403`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/863475eb9cd78ae6a4a22f1b90df7fe85e0af438/vllm/model_executor/model_loader/weight_cache/daemon.py#L399-L403)) finds no mismatched field and serves A's tensors. The engine never reads B from disk and logs no warning, while the CLI and the API `model` field both say B. The [docs](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/863475eb9cd78ae6a4a22f1b90df7fe85e0af438/docs/features/preload.md?plain=1#L21-L23) promise a "Safe fallback" when the daemon's cached weights don't match the engine, and say the fingerprint covers "checkpoint content". A user would therefore expect a daemon that still holds a different checkpoint to be rejected. Make two checkpoints that differ only in weight values. `q` is `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`; `q_mod` is a copy with `model.norm.weight` zeroed and the safetensors header untouched. `run_engine.py`: Without a daemon, each checkpoint gives its own output: With a daemon holding `q`, an engine started on `q_mod` gives `q`'s output: The engine log shows the weights came from the daemon, and neither process logs a warning: `hash_checkpoint()` returns the same value for any two checkpoints with the same tensor layout: For `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` the hashed header is 35,560 bytes of a 1,503,300,328-byte file (0.0024%). title: Engine crash: "Cannot get N free blocks" allocating the hot region at admission under GPU-pool pressure
body: vLLM main @ `93dd80f636`, 1× B200, Model Runner V2 (`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`). Also reproduces on #55398 before and after merging main. Under HiSparse GPU-pool pressure, admitting a new request can crash the engine in `HiSparseHotManager.allocate_new_blocks`: admission does not count the request's hot region (4 blocks here), then allocation fails. The engine is dead afterwards (`EngineDeadError`). **Repro** (shrunk GLM-5.3 config with dummy weights: 8 layers, hidden 256, 8 heads, 8 experts, `index_topk=128`, quantization removed): - `AsyncLLM`, `enforce_eager=True`, `block_size=64`, `max_model_len=8192`, `max_num_seqs=2`, `max_num_batched_tokens=4096`, `num_gpu_blocks_override=160` - attention backend `FLASHMLA_SPARSE`, `kv_cache_dtype=fp8_ds_mla`, `hisparse_config={"eager_host_mirror": true}` - `MultiConnector` kv_consumer: `HiSparseConnector` (`host_pool_gib=4`) + `NixlConnector` Steps: 1. Submit two concurrent ~6k-token prompts; neither gets admitted. Abort them after 20 s. 2. Submit a 4k-token prompt that shares a prefix with an aborted one; it is never admitted either. Abort it after 20 s. 3. Submit a tiny prompt with `max_tokens=3000`. The engine crashes with the traceback above. Found while investigating a different report on #55398; that report's crash (`HiSparse swap rows exceed the configured speculative decode capacity`) did not reproduce, but this one reproduces on every build tried. #59282 does not touch this path.
